A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same association-benchmark study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations and human results on OCL, Pangea, and HMDB, together with memory-strategy and data-filtering experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds GPT-4o evaluations on the single-step association and deduction tasks.

M1.justification: The dataset-construction procedure, association/deduction loop, data refinement, and StructM/NLM/ChainM mechanisms are retained. Revised Section 3 and new Algorithm 1 explain the existing procedure without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same OCL attributes and affordances, Pangea actions, and supplementary HMDB actions under the retained task scenarios. The HMDB experiment moves from Appendix D to F; the benchmark examples in new related-work figures are not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: v2 adds GPT-4o to the single-step comparisons in Tables 1 and 5–7, alongside the retained open-source models and Gemini-1.5-Flash. Comparator membership in the multi-step, perception, and HMDB experiments remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The two-candidate evaluation, task modes, filtering threshold, success-ratio and max/mean-step metrics, and example-size settings are retained. Algorithm 1 newly documents candidate randomization, memory resets, and asynchronous switching; it does not report a revision to the existing experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The example-size ablation, filtered/unfiltered comparisons, failure cases, and attention analysis are retained. New Appendix C and Figure 10 provide conceptual explanations rather than additional measured ablations or robustness tests; Figure 6 redisplays the attention analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain max/mean-step summaries and results from three human experts. v2 adds no concrete run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; Algorithm 1's symbolic N reiterates the existing multi-round evaluation.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 5–7 add GPT-4o results and revise cross-model averages. Its NLM attribute/affordance scores are 89.87/86.76, exceeding the retained Gemini scores of 88.39/85.40. Other existing result tables are unchanged. New summaries contain inconsistencies: Table 1 reports an affordance/StructM average of 61.25 and GPT-4o attribute/ChainM of 78.86, whereas the listed entries average 78.32 and Table 5 reports 79.86, respectively.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and the mathematical task definitions are retained. The expanded explanations and evaluation pseudocode introduce no new theorem, proof, derivation, or substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: an annotation-free association benchmark, three task levels, adjective/verb concepts, and a substantial model–human gap. The additional comparator evidence does not redefine these main claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix C and Figure 10 extend the explanation of the model–human gap through localized retrieval of relevant context, implicit commonsense reasoning, and short-term memory. These are explicitly speculative additions to the existing attention, contextual-understanding, and training-data explanations; Section 6's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.3 and Algorithm 1 disclose memory resets, randomized candidate ordering, the asynchronous switch condition, and conditional deduction for memory-enabled modes. Figure 7 supplies verification-prompt wording, and Figure 6 connects attention positions to concrete inputs. Existing memory weights, hardware information, and code/data access statements are retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix B and Figure 9 substantially expand positioning beyond the earlier brief related-work discussion. They compare capabilities with LLaVA-Bench, CompBench, SpatialRGPT, MMVP, MILEBENCH, and MARVEL; Appendix C also engages MMRA. The added discussion argues distinctions involving concept depth, sequential inputs, memory, and inductive/deductive reasoning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized revisions to the method and analysis prose, inserts Appendix A.3 and new Appendices B–C, and renumbers the retained appendices. It also updates the publication header, affiliation, and acknowledgments. Most existing prose and the main narrative order remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual explanation: Figures 1 and 6 are redesigned, Figures 7, 9, and 10 are added, and Algorithm 1 introduces a procedural display. Tables 1 and 5–7 expand for GPT-4o. The existing human-interface figure is retained as Figure 8, with accompanying table and figure repositioning.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful comparator evidence and documents evaluation control flow missing from v1, while revised diagrams and benchmark comparisons clarify the task. The gain is limited by newly inconsistent numerical summaries, including Table 1's 61.25 average instead of 78.32, and Appendix E.1's unrevised assertion that Gemini consistently performs best despite the added GPT-4o results. The retained central evidence remains intact, supporting a modest net improvement.
